verdict.rationale: Devin's docs say a task can be handed off to a cloud session that gets its own VM with a shell, browser and full repo access, and that it keeps running after you close your laptop. Independent tasks can also run at the same time. Community reports back this up hands-on: users describe Devin working for long stretches, even days, with a configurable max work time, and checking in periodically. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of the cloud VM's isolation and security boundaries.

support.subject: As a developer, I can delegate longer-running coding tasks to run in the background in an isolated cloud environment

citations.quote: The cloud session gets its own VM with a shell, browser, and full repo access, so it can keep going after you close your laptop.
Hand a task off to a cloud Devin session and keep working locally.
Carve out independent tasks and run them simultaneously.
You can set a 'max work time' before Devin pauses so it won't go for days endlessly spending your credits.
